statements.statement: Introduce the project before the team credits.
VineWeave Canopy combines climbing plants with a tree-like support to provide pedestrian shade.
Our group connects parametric geometry, material and construction choices, and shading analysis.
The names below identify our responsibilities.
We will explain both the design decisions and the evidence supporting them.
First, the final geometry and its drawing definitions.
The cover retains the core allocation; the planning document records the complete supplied descriptions.
Define the final geometry—and how it is measured
Dimensioned plan/elevation views; a final parameter schedule, separate from sensitivity settings.
Model records P1 and supplemental geometric check.
Curved support inclination is defined by its endpoint chord, not a local tangent.
*Angle of each ground-reaching centre-line endpoint chord.
Final dimensions need explicit definitions and readable technical views.
The final geometry has an overall height of about three point four eight metres and a plan extent of six point two two by six point six six metres.
Its approximate maximum horizontal exterior span is six point nine one metres.
For these curved supports, inclination is defined by the endpoint chord above horizontal.
The accompanying drawing sheets explain that definition and the measured range.
Next, link those features to environmental potential.
It is the maximum pair distance in the projected exterior mesh, not a foliage diameter or net usable width.
How the canopy can improve pedestrian comfort
Three physical pathways, with the strength of evidence shown next to each.
Arrows are conceptual; no temperature or airflow field is simulated.
Direct sun on people and ground
Open sides retain possible air paths.
Dense foliage can also add resistance.
Evapotranspiration may exchange latent heat; it needs healthy, watered plants.
Follow the sunlight, air and plant-water arrows; only shade is quantified here.
The crown and foliage intercept direct sun before it reaches people and the ground.
The solar arrows identify the pathway quantified in our optical scenarios.
Blue arrows show potential air paths through open sides, not a simulated wind improvement.
The dashed plant-water arrows indicate possible evapotranspiration, which depends on healthy plants and water.
Denser foliage can also resist airflow.
Material assignment follows the structural roles.
Do these arrows show simulated temperature or wind?
They explain physical mechanisms; the project quantifies shade, not cooling degrees or wind speed.

We propose an eighty-by-four millimetre steel tube for supports and solid engineered bamboo for the crown.
